questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of India's domestic (economic) territory?
options: An Air India aircraft flying between London and New York
A fishing vessel run by an Indian resident in international waters
The World Bank office in New Delhi
An oil rig run by ONGC in India's Exclusive Economic Zone
questions.explanation: Offices of international organisations such as the World Bank are not part of India's domestic territory, even when they are located inside India.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. National income is the sum of factor incomes earned by normal residents.
2. Transfer payments are included in national income.
3. Net factor income from abroad is added to domestic income to get national income.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Transfer payments are not payments for productive services, so they are excluded.
NI = NDP at FC + NFIA
Statement 2 is therefore wrong.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): GDP at market price is greater than GDP at factor cost when net indirect taxes are positive.
Reason (R): GDP at MP = GDP at FC + Net Indirect Taxes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are false
questions.explanation: Net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies) are the only difference between the two measures.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II:
List I | List II
A. Income method | 1. Sum of final expenditures
B. Expenditure method | 2. Sum of factor incomes
C. Value added method | 3. Sum of value added by all producers
questions.explanation:
Each method measures the same flow at a different stage: income, spending and production.
Method | Measures
Income | Factor payments
Expenditure | Final spending

questions.text: Which of the following are excluded while estimating national income? (More than one option may be correct.)
questions.explanation: Second-hand sales and share purchases are not current production, and pensions are transfer payments. Imputed rent and government wages are included.

questions.text: 2011-12 is the base year of the current GDP series. Which organisation compiles it?

questions.passage:

India's real GDP grew 7.8% in 2025-26, led by services and construction. Private consumption, which accounts for well over half of GDP, grew steadily as rural demand recovered.
Economists caution that headline growth hides uneven gains. Real wages in several informal sectors have barely moved, and household savings in financial assets fell to a multi-year low.

questions.text: By roughly what percentage did nominal GDP grow from 2023-24 to 2024-25?
questions.passage:
Study the table below and answer the questions that follow.
Year | Nominal GDP (Rs lakh crore) | Real GDP (Rs lakh crore)
2023-24 | 295 | 173
2024-25 | 324 | 184

questions.text: What was the GDP deflator in 2024-25 (approximately)?
questions.explanation: GDP deflator = Nominal GDP / Real GDP x 100 = 324 / 184 x 100 = 176.1

questions.text: Which of the following statements about double counting is correct?
options: It occurs when intermediate goods are counted along with final goods
It occurs when exports are excluded
It is avoided by adding the value of intermediate goods
It arises only in the income method
questions.explanation:
Counting intermediate goods along with final goods counts the same value twice. The value added method avoids it.
Note: Only final goods enter GDP.

questions.text:
Note: Answer on the basis of the System of National Accounts 2008.
Which of the following is treated as capital formation?
options: Purchase of a car by a household for personal use
Construction of a new factory building
Payment of wages to factory workers
Purchase of raw material by a firm for current production
questions.explanation: Only the factory building adds to the stock of fixed capital. The household car is final consumption.
